race.name: GFNY Villavicencio
race.tagline: Fast Llanos roads give way to Puerto de Buenavista: 109 kilometers and 1,308 meters at Colombia's Andean edge.

vitals.start_format: Mass-start competitive long course with chip timing
vitals.registration: Online through the official GFNY race site
vitals.feed_zones: Official GFNY aid stations with hydration, food, technical, and medical support
vitals.cutoff_time: See current race guide and official course rules
route_options: Recreational medium route: see official race site

climate.description: Villavicencio is warm and humid year-round. April brings meaningful rain risk, and the transition from exposed plains to climbing magnifies heat and hydration errors.
challenges: Rapid effort change from plains to climbing

terrain.primary: Fast tropical plains with a decisive mountain climb
terrain.surface: Paved urban, plains, and mountain roads around Villavicencio and Restrepo.
features: A false-flat rollout from Parque Las Malocas
Fast roads across the Meta department
The sustained Puerto de Buenavista climb
A hot lower course at the edge of the Eastern Andes

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Colombia's cycling culture and a well-defined plains-to-mountain course rate highly. Inaugural execution and moderate global prestige keep it in Tier 2.

key_climbs: A false-flat rollout from Parque Las Malocas
Fast roads across the Meta department
The sustained Puerto de Buenavista climb
A hot lower course at the edge of the Eastern Andes
climb_profile.profile_type: Fast tropical plains with a decisive mountain climb
climb_profile.king_of_mountain: Puerto de Buenavista, where the fast plains race becomes a mountain race and pacing errors become visible immediately.

course_description.character: The race begins on the fast, warm roads of the Llanos before turning toward the Eastern Andes. Puerto de Buenavista supplies the decisive sustained climbing, making the course a contrast between group speed, tropical heat, and late climbing economy.
course_description.signature_challenge: Puerto de Buenavista, where the fast plains race becomes a mountain race and pacing errors become visible immediately.

logistics.airport: La Vanguardia Airport (VVC) serves Villavicencio; most international riders connect through Bogotá El Dorado (BOG) and travel by air or road.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay near Parque Las Malocas or central Villavicencio. Confirm race transfers and allow margin for Bogotá-to-Villavicencio travel disruption.
logistics.transport: Use official race-week instructions for packet pickup, start access, and bike transport.
logistics.food: Villavicencio offers abundant rice, grilled meat, plantain, fruit, and soups. Heat and humidity make pre-race hydration more important than heavy loading.

history.origin_story: GFNY announced its return to Colombia in June 2026 through a new Villavicencio race linking the Llanos with Puerto de Buenavista.
history.reputation: A new Colombian GFNY whose course and likely field are credible, but whose first-edition operations remain untested.

biased_opinion.summary: The race begins on the fast, warm roads of the Llanos before turning toward the Eastern Andes. Puerto de Buenavista supplies the decisive sustained climbing, making the course a contrast between group speed, tropical heat, and late climbing economy.
weaknesses: International access usually requires a Bogotá connection
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A compact but serious Colombian race where riders must arrive with both peloton speed and climbing durability.

final_verdict.one_liner: Fast Llanos roads give way to Puerto de Buenavista: 109 kilometers and 1,308 meters at Colombia's Andean edge.
final_verdict.should_you_race: A compact but serious Colombian race where riders must arrive with both peloton speed and climbing durability.
final_verdict.alternatives: GFNY Cali for a longer Colombian course, or Alto de Letras for a far more extreme climbing challenge.
